title: The big-name stocks in the crosshairs as trade-war
text:
The big-name stocks in the crosshairs as trade-war worries reboot 
MARKETWATCH 8:25 AM ET 3/14/2018 
Critical information for the U.S. trading day 

Trade-war worries, which have been buzzing around this market like a pesky fly for weeks, may have just gotten an unwelcome jolt of new life. 

Stocks, having recovered from the initial shock of the White House's steel tariff move, got rattled again late yesterday on talk of new, wider levies on Chinese goods. Strategists think it will take a full-blown trade war to take this market down ... and our call of the day from the Wolf Street blog's Wolf Richter says we should watch out. 

"If this is true ... then it's going to add a lot of fuel to the already heated trade dispute between the U.S. and China, and may ultimately make the steel and aluminum tariffs look like a game," he writes. 

Speculation over China tariffs surfaced last week ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-considers-tariffs-on-wide- range-of-chinese-imports-report-2018-03-07), but the latest chatter adds some detail -- up to $60 billion in tariffs ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-reportedly-eyes-60-billion-in-tariffs-on-china-goods-2018-03-13 ) could be imposed on tech products and imports such clothing. This comes after the Trump administration squashed a buyout of chip group Qualcomm (QCOM) by Broadcom (AVGO) on worries about China telecoms giant Huawei. 

"Concerns about the possibility of a trade war and concerns about the shutting down of one tech deal may be a precursor for others, and that may imply lower valuations for technology companies," Edward Koen, portfolio manager at QMA, told CNBC ( https://www.cnbc.com/2018/03/13/trump-shaking-up-market-but-only-trade-wars-would-bring-big-sell- off.html). 

Check out:If Broadcom-Qualcomm deal can't pass Trump's test, what can? ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/if-broadcom- qualcomm-deal-cant-pass-trumps-test-what-can-2018-03-13) 

As for where a China tariff could hit hard, Boeing (BA) , Apple (AAPL) , Micron (MU), Nvidia (NVDA) . Walmart (WMT) and Nike (NKE) have been mentioned here (ttps://www.investors.com/market-trend/stock-market-today/trump-china-tariffs- loom-putting-dow-jones-boeing-apple-intel-at-risk-sp-500-futures-fall/) and there ( https://www.bloomberg.com/news/ articles/2018-03-07/trump-s-china-levy-threat-puts-walmart-nike-suppliers-on-notice) as in line to take a hit. Boeing and Apple each fell yesterday. 

"We're not talking about fancy cashmere sweaters, we're talking about cotton T-shirts and jeans and shoes that kids wear for back-to-school," Hun Quach, a trade lobbyist for the Retail Industry Leaders Association tells Reuters (https:/ /www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trump-china/trump-eyes-tariffs-on-up-to-60-billion-chinese-goods-tech-telecoms-apparel- targeted-idUSKCN1GP2X8) of potentially higher tariffs on China. 

"Alarm bells are ringing," she says. 

Key market gauges 

Investors are looking out for retail sales data due this morning. Ahead of that, Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are stepping higher. Banking and tech stocks dragged Asian stocks ( https://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets- pull-back-led-by-banking-and-tec) ( https://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-pull-back-led-by-banking-and-tec ) south ( https://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-pull-back-led-by-banking-and-tec ). In Europe, shares got a bump from comments by ECB President Mario Draghi ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-flip-up-as-draghi-says- subdued-inflation-will-keep-bond-buys-in-place-2018-03-14), who spoke about stepping up bond buys. 

The dollar is moving up, with the euro dented by those Draghi remarks. Elsewhere, gold is off slightly, and oil is moving up. 

( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-fall-flat-to-start-march-2018-02-28)Check out Market Snapshot (http:/ /www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-shape-up-to-rebound-as-focus-turns-to-retail-sales-2018-03-14) for more on today's action. 

The buzz 

Walmart (WMT) wants to take on Kroger (KR) and Amazon (AMZN) when it comes to home-grocery delivery. The retailer plans to roll out deliveries in 100 cities by the end of the year. ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/walmart-offering- home-grocery-delivery-in-100-cities-to-compete-with-amazon-kroger-2018-03-14) 

It's another big day on the data front, with retail sales and producer prices coming at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, and business inventories at 10 a.m. Eastern. 

Read:The most important chart in the world, updated for February CPI data ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-most- important-chart-in-the-world-updated-for-february-cpi-data-2018-03-13) 

France plans to take Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google and Apple (AAPL) to court over "abusive trade practices," Finance Minister Bruno Le Maire told a radio program Wednesday ( https://www.reuters.com/article/us-apple-google-france/france- to-sue-google-apple-over-developer-contracts-minister-idUSKCN1GQ0SP). 

Mott Capital founder Michael Kramer wonders whether techs are starting to get overextended (https:// mottcapitalmanagement.com/there-may-be-no-tesla-killer-plus-amazon-nvidia-micron-netflix/), noting some analysts seem to be trying to find fresh ways to support price-target revisions. He points to Nvidia, which got a $300 price target from Jefferies earlier this week, on the rationale that a new Steven Spielberg movie could be a catalyst for VR headsets. 

Producers of Netflix's (NFLX) hit series "The Crown" are taking some flak after revelations the actress who plays Queen Elizabeth II is paid less than her on-screen husband ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/on-netflixs-the-crown-the- prince-got-paid-more-than-the-queen-2018-03-13). That will apparently be rectified going forward. 

Read:Netflix is poised to enter the TV news business ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-poised-to-enter-the- tv-news-business-2018-03-13) 

( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/netflix-is-poised-to-enter-the-tv-news-business-2018-03-13)Bitcoin got rattled after Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google signaled in an update to its ad T&Cs ( https://support.google.com/adwordspolicy/answer/ 7648803?hl=en&ref_topic=29265) that it plans to ban online ads for cryptocurrencies and ICOs in June. That comes as Google said it had blacklisted nearly 90,000 websites and 700,000 mobile apps ( https://blog.google/topics/ads/ advertising-ecosystem-works-everyone/) for breaking its ad rules. 

The chart 

Credit Suisse has rolled out its Global Investment Returns Yearbook for 2018. Among its findings, it appears equities have remained on top for decades, when it comes to returns. 

"Since 1900, global equities have beaten bonds and bills, outperforming cash (Treasury bills) by 4.3% and bonds by 3.2% a year -- a reward for the higher risk associated with investing in stocks," say the authors of the yearbook, put together by the Credit Suisse Research Institute and London Business School professors. 

The quote 

"Remembering Stephen Hawking, a renowned physicist and ambassador of science. His theories unlocked a universe of possibilities that we & the world are exploring. May you keep flying like superman in microgravity, as you said to astronauts on @Space_Station in 2014." -- That was NASA tweeting a tribute ( https://twitter.com/NASA/status/ 973787392590172160) to the renowned and beloved British scientist who died early Wednesday at the age of 76. 

That's one of tons of tributes pouring in ( http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-world-has-lost-a-beautiful-mind- tributes-pour-in-for-stephen-hawking-2018-03-14):

The stat 

1 million -- That's how many shoes Adidas sold in 2017 that were created from the growing swell of ocean plastic ( https://www.cnbc.com/2018/03/14/adidas-sold-1-million-shoes-made-out-of-ocean-plastic-in-2017.html ). The sportswear maker teamed up with Parley for the Oceans to create three new UltraBoost shoes, made out of leftover bottles and other discards.
